circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Located on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, the 5. 281-kilometer Yas Marina Circuit was designed by Hermann Tilke and has served as the venue for Formula One's season finale since 2009. The track became the second Middle Eastern circuit to join the F1 calendar, following Bahrain's earlier establishment and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track that loops around Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and hosts the annual Australian Grand Prix along with supporting motorsport events. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 licence, confirming its status as a premier international racing facility.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The 4. 326 km circuit in Spielberg, Austria, originally called Österreichring, held the Austrian Grand Prix annually from 1970 to 1987. Following reconstruction and renaming as the A1-Ring, it returned to hosting the prestigious event from 1997 to 2003.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital that spans 6. 003 km, ranking as the fourth-longest venue on the Formula One schedule. Following its debut as the European Grand Prix in 2016, the circuit has hosted the Azerbaijan Grand Prix annually since 2017.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit is a 5. 412 km venue that hosted the maiden Formula One race in the Middle East that same year and continues to stage the annual Bahrain Grand Prix alongside various other motorsport events. The FIA Grade 1 facility, which features multiple track configurations, has also accommodated GP2 racing, a one-time Australian V8 Supercar series called the Desert 400, and 24-hour endurance competitions.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, this 4. 657 km Spanish motorsport venue features a balanced mix of extended straights and diverse corner configurations that make it representative of general racing demands. The facility holds FIA Grade 1 certification and accommodates approximately 140,700 spectators.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian racing circuit, stretching over 7 kilometres through the Walloon region near Stavelot, has been a Formula One fixture since the sport's inaugural 1950 season. The venue has continuously hosted the Belgian Grand Prix annually since 1985, with only two absences in 2003 and 2006, making it one of motorsport's most enduring championship venues.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361 km circuit hosts the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix and has accommodated various other international racing series including sportscar championships and North American racing competitions throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Located in Shanghai's Jiading District, this Chinese motorsport facility hosted the Formula One Chinese Grand Prix annually from 2004 until 2019, with the race returning to the calendar from 2024 onward. The venue has expanded its motorsport portfolio to include electric racing events alongside its traditional Grand Prix hosting duties.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone is a racing venue located in the English Midlands that has served as the permanent home of Britain's Formula One Grand Prix since 1987, though it previously alternated with two other circuits during the 1955-1986 period. The track holds significant historical importance as the venue for the inaugural World Championship round in 1950 and has continuously hosted international motorsport since its inaugural F1 event in 1948.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, located near Budapest in Mogyoród, hosted Formula One's inaugural Eastern Bloc Grand Prix in 1986 after Bernie Ecclestone sought a race venue behind the Iron Curtain. Built in just eight months starting October 1985, the 4. 381 km circuit was constructed outside the city near a highway rather than as a street course in Budapest's main park, and its inaugural race commemorated János Drapál, Hungary's pioneering motorcycle Grand Prix champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, Monza is a 5. 793 km circuit constructed in 1922 and ranks among Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venues. The track has hosted the Italian Grand Prix virtually every year since 1949, making it one of Formula One's most enduring fixtures, and earns its nickname "Temple of Speed" through its characteristically fast layout featuring extended straights and high-velocity corners.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Located in Mie Prefecture, Japan, the Suzuka Circuit is a 5. 807 km track operated by Honda Mobilityland that hosts prestigious motorsport events. The venue is most renowned for staging Formula One Grands Prix and Japanese Super Formula races, accommodating up to 155,000 spectators.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street course laid out through Paradise, Nevada, that incorporates the famous Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding thoroughfares, creating a route that passes by iconic casino resorts and entertainment venues. The track weaves through the heart of the city's hospitality district, featuring prominent landmarks such as major hotels and entertainment complexes along its path.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez is a 4. 304 km circuit honoring racing brothers Ricardo and Pedro Rodríguez, both of whom died in racing accidents during the 1960s and 1970s. The track has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, though it previously staged the event on a different configuration until 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary racing facility constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners that produces qualifying speeds near 139 mph. Designed by specialist circuit architects for the Miami Grand Prix's debut on the Formula One calendar in 2022, the track has since welcomed additional racing series to its venue.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street track that winds through the Monte Carlo and La Condamine districts, following the waterfront layout of the Principality of Monaco. It is typically known as Monte Carlo, reflecting that the majority of the course traverses the Monte Carlo neighbourhood.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: This 4. 259 km Dutch racing circuit sits in the coastal dunes near Amsterdam and hosted the Dutch Grand Prix following its return to Formula One in 2021, a partnership that concluded in 2026. The track, located north of Zandvoort close to the North Sea, has operated under various names throughout its history, most recently adopting a sponsorship designation from mid-2025.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: The Lusail International Circuit is situated near Lusail, Qatar, north of Doha, and spans 5. 419 kilometres with a 1. 068-kilometre main straight.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Interlagos, situated in São Paulo, Brazil, is a 4. 309 km counterclockwise racing venue that opened in 1940 and was later renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace following his fatal aviation accident. The circuit complex additionally features a karting facility dedicated to fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street track situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coastline that has hosted the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix since 2021. The venue began accommodating additional international racing series starting in 2025.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit winds through Singapore's urban landscape, traversing the Downtown Core and Kallang districts while circling Marina Bay.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located in Montmeló near Barcelona, the Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya stretches 4. 657 kilometers and features a balanced blend of extended straights and diverse corner sequences, making it a comprehensive test of driver and vehicle capability. The venue holds an FIA Grade 1 license and can accommodate 140,700 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the venue hosts major international racing series including NASCAR, MotoGP, and the Lone Star Le Mans endurance event, while having previously accommodated various other motorsport championships.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a racing driver of Thai and British nationality who represents Thailand in Formula One, currently driving for Williams.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Fernando Alonso, a Spanish driver competing for Aston Martin, stands as a two-time Formula One World Champion, having claimed titles in 2005 and 2006 during his tenure at Renault, and has accumulated 32 Grand Prix victories across 23 seasons. Beyond Formula One, Alonso achieved remarkable success in endurance racing, winning the 2018-19 FIA World Endurance Championship and capturing the 24 Hours of Le Mans twice with Toyota, making him the sole driver to have secured both a Formula One World Championship and a World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli made his Formula One debut in 2025 and currently races for Mercedes, where he has secured eight race victories to date.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British motorsport competitor currently racing in Formula One with the Haas team. He has established himself as a driver on the sport's premier racing circuit.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races in Formula One as a member of the Audi team. Known for his competitive performances, he has established himself as part of the manufacturer's racing program.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the grid. His career highlights include two runner-up finishes in the drivers' championship while with Mercedes, along with 10 Grand Prix victories accumulated across his time in the sport.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto is an Argentine racing driver currently competing in Formula One with Alpine.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan, an Australian driver, holds a reserve role with Haas in Formula One while actively competing in European Le Mans Series prototypes for Nielsen Racing. He has participated in seven Grand Prix events during the 2024-2025 season.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly, a French driver currently racing for Alpine, achieved his sole Formula One victory at the 2020 Italian Grand Prix while competing for AlphaTauri.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver with French and Algerian heritage, races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British Formula One driver competing for Ferrari who has secured seven World Drivers' Championship titles, matching Michael Schumacher's record. He holds multiple competitive records including the most race victories, pole positions, and podium finishes in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: German driver Nicolas Hülkenberg currently races in Formula One for Audi. Beyond single-seater competition, he achieved success in endurance racing by winning the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 alongside Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson is a New Zealand motorsport driver currently competing in Formula One with the Racing Bulls team.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: Charles Leclerc, a Monégasque driver racing for Ferrari, finished second in the 2022 drivers' championship and has claimed nine career victories across nine seasons in Formula One.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Kevin Magnussen is a Danish driver currently competing in the FIA World Endurance Championship with WRT as a BMW factory driver, while also taking on part-time NASCAR commitments with Trackhouse Racing. His Formula One career spanned two separate periods between 2014 and 2024, with a gap from 2021 to 2022.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: British driver Lando Norris secured the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship while racing for McLaren, adding to his total of 13 Grand Prix victories accumulated over eight seasons in the sport.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon currently races for Haas in Formula One after previously competing for Alpine, where he achieved his sole grand prix victory at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez competes in Formula One for Cadillac, bringing over 15 seasons of experience to the grid. He achieved second place in the 2023 World Drivers' Championship while driving for Red Bull and has accumulated six race victories throughout his career.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri, an Australian driver, currently races for McLaren in Formula One. Throughout his four seasons in the sport, he has secured victories in nine Grand Prix events.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known as "the Honey Badger," competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight race victories during his career in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having accumulated eight race victories throughout his career spanning eight seasons.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, where he has claimed four Grand Prix victories throughout his 12-year career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: Logan Sargeant is an American driver who raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing. He currently competes in the FIA World Endurance Championship's LMGT3 category for Proton Competition, having previously driven LMP2 cars in IMSA competition.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian racing driver currently competing in Formula One for Aston Martin, where he brings his motorsport experience to the grid.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda is a Japanese driver currently functioning as a reserve for both Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls in Formula One. After competing as a full-time driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a backup role beginning in 2026.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch racing driver Max Verstappen has claimed four consecutive Formula One World Drivers' Championships between 2021 and 2024 while competing for Red Bull Racing. Across his 12-season career, he has accumulated 71 Grand Prix victories, establishing himself as one of the sport's most dominant performers.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu is the sole Chinese driver to have competed in Formula One, with an active racing presence spanning from 2022 through 2024. He currently holds a reserve driver position with the Cadillac Formula One team.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team operated as Renault's factory squad from 2021 onwards under the Alpine brand, following a rebranding that highlighted the luxury sports car marque. Renault maintained its works team status with Alpine until withdrawing from the championship at the conclusion of 2025.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has competed in Formula One through multiple incarnations as a British manufacturer, with the current operation run by AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari HP represents the motorsport arm of the Italian luxury automaker Ferrari and fields entries in Formula One competition. Recognized by the "Prancing Horse" emblem, the team holds the distinction of being both the longest-running and most accomplished competitor in the sport, having participated continuously since the World Championship's inaugural 1950 season.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: American entrepreneur Gene Haas founded this Formula One outfit in 2014, with the team competing from 2016 onward. Ayao Komatsu has led the squad as team principal since January 2024, succeeding Guenther Steiner who held the position throughout the team's first eight seasons.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Swiss-based Sauber Motorsport emerged from Peter Sauber's 1970 engineering venture and became an independent Formula One constructor starting in 1993, achieving notable success in endurance racing including the 1989 Le Mans 24 Hours victory. After 32 years of competition and becoming the fourth-longest-running constructor by race entries, the team departed Formula One in 2025 when Audi acquired its assets to establish their own championship entry.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren is a British Formula One outfit headquartered in Woking that competes under the McLaren Mastercard banner. The team operates as part of the McLaren Group and is ultimately owned by Mumtalakat Holding Company.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: The Mercedes-AMG Petronas Formula One Team, based in Brackley and holding a German racing licence, represents Mercedes-Benz's continuous involvement in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier. Following a 2020 agreement, the team became jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and team principal Toto Wolff from January 2022. Mercedes-branded racing teams are traditionally known as the "Silver Arrows.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team and constructor that commenced operations in 2024, representing the second squad under Red Bull's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Operating from Faenza with an additional facility near its sister team in Milton Keynes, the squad functions as part of the Austrian conglomerate's two-team strategy in the sport.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced operations in 2024 as part of Red Bull's two-team structure alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the team operates as a secondary Red Bull entity within the championship.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing, an Austrian-licensed team headquartered in England, has been a prominent Formula One competitor since 2005. The squad forms part of Red Bull GmbH's motorsport portfolio alongside Racing Bulls, and was steered by Christian Horner throughout its two-decade tenure before Laurent Mekies assumed leadership in 2025.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, a British Formula One constructor established in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head, evolved from Frank's earlier failed racing venture. Currently operating as Atlassian Williams F1 Team for 2026, the outfit is headquartered at its Grove facility in Oxfordshire.
